newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-PAKISTAN SHOCKED BY SOHAIL SUSPENSION.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTAN SHOCKED BY SOHAIL SUSPENSION.

text.p: The Pakistan cricket team were shocked on Friday by a one-match suspension for dissent handed to opener Aamir Sohail, who will miss Saturday's first game of the World Series limited overs final against West Indies.
The suspensino handed down by the Australian Cricket Board added another entry to Sohail's growing disciplinary record.
"He's our main player, it's tough news," Pakistan captain Wasim Akram told reporters after arriving in Sydney ahead of the first of the best-of-three finals series.

"I only heard a little while ago so I'm still in a little shock. We are definitely going to miss Aamir tomorrow, but I believe we have to carry on and we'll wait for him for the next game," Akram said.

Sohail was reported by match referee Raman Subba Row for his reaction after being dismissed during Pakistan's three-wicket loss to Australia on Thursday. Subba Row announced his decision after conducting a hearing into the incident in Melbourne.
Akram said he thought the penalty was harsh but described Sohail as hot-tempered.
"Aamir has a bad temper, he's a hot-tempered guy," Akram said. "He got out to what was an illegal delivery like everybody else thought and he was just a little upset."
Sohail was clearly unhappy with his dismissal for six runs and appeared to gesticulate towards umpires Darryl Hair and Peter Parker as he walked back to the pavilion.

The left-handed batsman hooked a short-pitched ball from fast bowler Anthony Stuart to give Darren Lehmann a simple catch at fine leg but it was apparent the opener believed the delivery should have been called a no-ball because it bounced above shoulder height.
Fourteen months ago, Subba Row fined Sohail half his match fee and handed him a two-match suspended sentence for throwing his bat during the second test against Australia in Hobart.
At the limited overs World Cup in Australia in 1992, Sohail was fined US$250 for misconduct after he disputed his dismissal against Australia in Perth.
